subject: ACME Health — scope for inspection access & Article 30 excerpt
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <compliance@acme-health.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Marco Bianchi <m.bianchi@acme-health.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T14:03:00Z
Subject: Request: Article 30 extract + inspection access for DPIA review

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. ACME's privacy team has a couple of follow-ups so we can complete our DPIA and internal audit:

1) A short excerpt of your Article 30 register covering processing activities for ACME (fields + sample records) we can include in our submission. Redaction of other customers is expected.
2) Clarification on the transfer mechanism you propose for EU data — we need your recommended controls (SCCs, onshore routing, or adequacy justification).
3) One-time inspector access: our auditor needs to validate logging and retention settings for a sampled set of requests. Ideally a remote, time-boxed review with an observer account — what options do you support?

Can you share an example Article 30 excerpt and a proposed process for the inspection? Also confirm who at Redwood will own scheduling and evidence delivery.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Privacy — ACME Health
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <compliance@acme-health.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-13T08:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Article 30 extract + inspection access for DPIA review

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely support each item. High-level plan below and attached a redacted Article 30 excerpt for ACME to review (redacted-article30-excerpt.pdf).

Plan (summary):
- Article 30: provide a redacted CSV + human-readable excerpt. See attachments.
- Transfer mechanism: default to SCCs for the EU -> US processing leg; we can offer optional onshore execution (EU-region runtime) for particularly sensitive workloads.
- Inspector access: two paths — (A) remote time-boxed secure session where the auditor views logs/screenshare within our EU region environment, or (B) ephemeral auditor API account with strictly scoped read-only access and IP allowlist, audited via session recordings. Both require NDA + session terms.

I've looped in Karthik (data protection) and Naomi (ops evidence) to confirm technical feasibility and a proposed timeline. Proposed next step: Naomi to propose two windows next week for a 90-minute session.

Action items:
- Karthik: confirm SCC template and whether we can provide a signed statement of execution controls.
- Naomi: prepare anonymised processing-map-anonymised.csv and inspector-access-runbook.docx.
- Marissa: provide requested Article 30 excerpt (attached) and draft session T&Cs.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-13T12:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Article 30 extract + inspection access for DPIA review

Thanks — quick technical notes below.

1) SCCs vs onshore execution: Our standard approach when customers ask for the strongest guarantees is to combine SCCs with EU-region execution for the data plane. For ACME's case (health sector), recommend the EU-region runtime option: it eliminates cross-border token/session writes and simplifies audit artifacts. We should present both options with tradeoffs (cost + latency).

2) Art 30 excerpt: redacted excerpt fine. Provide a schema mapping file (processing-map-anonymised.csv) with pseudonymised sample rows rather than full PD. That will satisfy their DPIA reviewers most of the time.

3) Inspector access: I'd prefer path B (ephemeral auditor account) with the following constraints:
- 8-hour temporary credential window per audit session
- read-only access limited to logs/trace view and relevant S3 export manifest
- enforced IP allowlist for ACME auditor IPs
- session recorded and stored immutably for our compliance review

We should also flag that live queries against production cost tokens; Naomi please estimate the operational delta.

Karthik
Director, Applied Privacy
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-14T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Article 30 extract + inspection access for DPIA review

All — attached is the anonymised processing map and the runbook for inspector sessions (inspector-access-runbook.docx). Quick operational notes:

- We can provision ephemeral auditor credentials via our access-portal. Typical lead time 48 hours for provisioning + NDA verification.
- Cost/impact: a single 4-8 hour evaluation in EU region increases snapshot exports and small trace queries; estimate ~€120 operational overhead (one-off) — we can absorb or pass depending on contract.
- Evidence we can provide during session: audit ledger subset (article30 rows), request/response traces (pseudonymised), KV cache access patterns, retention settings.
- We will not export raw customer payloads; all sample records will be pseudonymised.

Proposed timeline:
- Thu 2026-08-19 09:00–11:00 CET (session A) OR
- Mon 2026-08-23 14:00–16:00 CET (session B)

If those work, I'll draft the session T&Cs and the ephemeral access checklist.

—Naomi
Senior Technical Program Manager, Evidence & Onboarding

2) Confirm which session window you prefer (Thu 19th 09:00–11:00 CET or Mon 23rd 14:00–16:00 CET).
